title: Lanes and staggers on a 400 m track
body: A standard 400 m athletics track has two straight sections of 84.39 m each and two semicircular bends with a common centre on each side. The innermost semicircle on each bend has radius 36.5 m, and each lane is 1.22 m wide. A runner is assumed to run 0.3 m from the inner border of her lane. In the innermost lane she runs two straights (168.78 m) and two semicircles of radius 36.8 m, which together make a full circle of circumference 2 × 3.1416 × 36.8 = 231.22 m, giving 400 m in all. A runner in the second lane runs the same straights, but her bends have a radius that is larger by one lane width. To make the race fair, her start line is moved ahead by a distance called the stagger.
